newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium sticks to cautious 2.1 pct 1997 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Belgium sticks to cautious 2.1 pct 1997 GDP growth.

text.p: The Belgian government said on Tuesday it based its 1997 budget calculations on an unchanged, cautious growth forecast for real gross domestic product (GDP) of 2.1 percent.
"The expected growth figure of 2.1 percent for 1997 was not adjusted to the last more optimistic forecasts," Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene told parliament.

Budget Minister Herman Van Rompuy later told a news conference the 2.1 percent forecast was below a forecast of 2.3 to 2.4 percent by the European Commission, OECD and the IMF, and below the Belgian High Council of Finance's 2.4 percent.
"We incorporated a safety margin...our figure for GDP is below the average...it was on the cautious side," Van Rompuy said.

He added that as another safety measure, the government had drafted the 1997 budget based on the assumption that short-term interest rates could rise to 4.1 percent -- compared with the current 3.0 to 3.1 percent.
"This will save us from any possible setbacks," he said.
